podcast-tuckercarlson-f72Tc-iXc4A:
Tucker Carlson gives his reply to President Joe Biden's State of the Union address. He speaks live on his own network right after the speech ends. His verdict is harsh from the first minute.

Carlson calls the address dark, cruel, and split against fellow citizens. He says Biden attacked rivals more than he offered hope. He compares early lines in the speech to past strongman rhetoric. The episode works as a full counter-speech for viewers who wanted the other side at once, without waiting for next-day news panels. He closes by urging viewers to judge the speech themselves.
uslaw-usc-t2-s164a: Section 164a of Title 2 of the United States Code deals with the spread of a work of the Library of Congress. It sits in Chapter 5, on the Library of Congress. The work in view is the index and the short form of the laws of the states. Those works are let through by Section 164 of the title. The Librarian of Congress is told to have them printed and bound. The spread of the books is for the use of the state alone.
uslaw-usc-t2-s1824a:
Section 1824a of Title 2 of the United States Code, in the chapter on the Architect of the Capitol, requires a program for collecting and selling recyclable materials. The materials come from the Capitol buildings and grounds. The Architect must run the program under the procedures that govern sales of surplus property by an executive agency. Materials already covered by other named collection and sale programs are excluded.

A revolving fund for the Architect's office is established in the Treasury. It consists of proceeds from sales under the program, plus such amounts as may be appropriated to it. The fund structure lets money earned from selling recyclables flow back into running the program, rather than lapsing at the end of a fiscal year.
uslaw-usc-t2-s194a:
Section 194a of Title 2 of the United States Code lets congressional committees ask federal foreign-affairs staff for their views. Oversight of foreign policy needs candor from the officers who run it. This section opens a channel for their opinions.

Upon the request of a committee of either House, the duty arises. A joint committee of Congress, or a member of such a committee, may also make the request. The persons addressed are officers or employees of the federal departments and agencies concerned. Their field is foreign countries or multilateral organizations, as the title states. They are asked for an expression of views and opinions, as the text continues. The section gives Congress a stated right to hear judgment, not only facts, from the government's own foreign service.
